name: Jellied Veal
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Cover with water and cook a shank of veal slowly until the meat comes easily from the bones
Meanwhile hard-boil two eggs and chill in cold water
Moisten a mould, cut the eggs in slices and lay in the bottom
Take out the bones and gristle and pour the remainder on the eggs
Put in a cool place, or on ice, and it will jelly quickly

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cover with water and cook a shank of veal slowly until the meat comes easily from the bones
2. Season with salt and pepper
3. Meanwhile hard-boil two eggs and chill in cold water
4. Moisten a mould, cut the eggs in slices and lay in the bottom
5. Take out the bones and gristle and pour the remainder on the eggs
6. Put in a cool place, or on ice, and it will jelly quickly
